Subject: Follow-up: retention SLAs, backups, and vendor questionnaire for MedNova

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on retention/deletion expectations and the security questionnaire:

Recap (from our discussion)
- Primary requirement: ability to specify deletion SLO for customer data and a clear policy for backups/snapshots and audit logs.
- Compliance needs: SOC 2 Type II evidence, GDPR data subject request timelines, and HIPAA controls for PHI (MedNova has PHI in-scope).
- Backup concerns: MedNova needs clarity on backup retention vs. primary data deletion and whether cold copies are considered recoverable backups for SLA purposes.

Proposed answers / next steps (action owners in parentheses)
1) Deletion SLA: Redwood supports a configurable deletion SLA; default is 30 days for primary datasets unless otherwise contracted (Lauren). We will propose contract language for inclusion in the Dedicated/Private offering. (attached: Redwood_Retention_SLA_Draft.pdf)
2) Backup retention: Backups (snapshots) are retained separately; default snapshot retention is 90 days. For HIPAA/regulated customers we offer options to shorten or extend retention and to request controlled deletion of backups within a 90-day window via an escalation process (Neha).
3) Log retention: Audit logs are retained for 365 days by default. We can discuss shorter retention for privacy reasons or longer retention for forensic requirements (Neha).
4) SOC 2 / evidence: We will provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report through an NDA channel (Marissa).
5) Vendor questionnaire: I attached your questionnaire (MedNova_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire-v1.docx). Neha, can you confirm who on security should own populating this?

Please see the attached draft SLA and the questionnaire. If anything above is incorrect, flag it and I’ll update. Suggested next steps:
- Neha to confirm backup deletion workflow and provide a short note on how snapshots are treated for deletion requests (by Thu 1/14).
- Marissa to share SOC 2 report link under NDA (ETA 1/15).
- Tom to confirm whether MedNova requires immutable backups or special retention hold windows for legal holds.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate signatures/contract language once we have the retention numbers locked.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so we can route this internally:

1) HIPAA in-scope: Yes. Any PHI stored via the integration is in scope. We need to confirm Redwood's BA agreement approach — do you have a standard BAA or is that on a case-by-case basis?
2) Deletion SLA: Our legal team prefers a hard 30-day delete for primary data with certification (signed statement) that data is removed from active storage. Backups are a secondary concern — we need to understand if backups are restorable after deletion or if you support scrub/expire that makes data unrecoverable.
3) Immutable backups / legal hold: For now, MedNova wants the option to place a 120-day legal hold that prevents deletion for specific datasets if needed. We also want an option for immutability on snapshots for a specified window.

Also — LegalOps asked if we can move the vendor questionnaire into a fillable PDF or provide an online form. They're tight on calendar this week.

Can you confirm whether Redwood encrypts backups with customer-managed keys and whether key rotation impacts backup recovery windows?

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Infrastructure & Security Operations
MedNova Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@mednova.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, LegalOps <legalops@mednova.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 10:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: retention SLAs, backups, and vendor questionnaire for MedNova

Tom — thanks for the questions. Below are direct answers and a short note on implementation constraints. Happy to hop on a follow-up call if helpful.

SOC 2 / BAA
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering security, availability, and confidentiality for our hosted and dedicated control planes. We will share the report via secure link once NDA/standard non-disclosure is in place (Marissa will send).
- BAA: We support a standard BAA for HIPAA customers. We include BAA terms as an addendum to the contract for Dedicated/Private deployments; our legal team prefers to review specifics for Private (on-prem/VPC) cases.

Deletion SLA & Backups
- Primary data deletion: Redwood supports a configurable deletion SLA; default contract language proposes a 30-calendar-day removal from active storage and dependent caches. We will provide a certificate of deletion upon request.
- Backups/snapshots: Snapshots are retained independently from primary storage. Default snapshot retention is 90 days. Important: snapshots are kept as point-in-time images and may contain data that predates the deletion request. We can offer an expedited backlog scrub under a contract clause (typically 90 days) — but immediate purging of older snapshots is operationally complex and requires a contractual commitment and escalation path.
- Immutable snapshots / legal holds: We can support immutability flags on snapshots for defined windows (e.g., 30/90/120 days) for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted API customers we provide a managed legal-hold workflow with documented timelines and an SLA for preservation.

Encryption & KMS
- Backups are encrypted at rest using KMS-managed keys. For Private/Dedicated customers we support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key) for both primary and backup encryption. Key rotation is supported and does not, by itself, render backups unrecoverable — rotations are performed with a rewrap process and documented procedures.

Logs & Audit Trails
- Default audit log retention: 365 days. We can customize retention down to 90 days or up to multi-year retention with an enterprise agreement. Log writes are append-only; deletion requests for logs follow our internal retention policy and are audited.

Next steps (owner + ETA)
- Neha to prepare a short technical appendix describing the backup scrub/expunge process and timelines (ETA: 1/15).
- Marissa to circulate SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and confirm BAA template (ETA: 1/15).
- Lauren to provide target legal hold windows and whether MedNova expects immutability for all snapshots or a per-dataset option (Tom action).

I will also start the vendor questionnaire intake (prefer docx is fine; we can convert to a fillable PDF for LegalOps) — if you can provide preferred format I will prioritize it.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
